_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: Shelley takes picks only from its opener, and picking skips the toolbar. The test opens Shelley from the bookmarklet as a user would: it takes the bookmarklet from Shelley, then clicks it on a page on another origin, http://host.test/ (title "Host Page", a main with an h1 "Host Page", a paragraph #para "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." and a list ul.list of "First item" and "Second item"), with that paragraph selected. The bookmarklet adds a toolbar to the host page, the element "shelley-bookmarklet", whose controls are in its open shadow root: a status span ".status" and the buttons Record, Pick, Shelley and Close. It opens Shelley in a popup, tab "popup", "the Shelley window". "The toolbar status" is the ".status" element in the toolbar: {"within": {"selector": "shelley-bookmarklet"}, "selector": ".status"} (selectors reach into open shadow roots, but a combinator like "shelley-bookmarklet .status" does not cross into one). Pick the toolbar's buttons by role "button" and exact accessible name, also with "within" the toolbar. Opening it: 1. Navigate to /new. 2. Click the button whose accessible name contains "More options". 3. The overflow menu's bookmarklet item is the bookmarklet too: keep its link, which must be a javascript: URL, with eval (window.__href = document.querySelector('[data-testid=bookmarklet-menu-item]')?.getAttribute('href') ?? '').startsWith('javascript:') expecting true. 4. Click [data-testid="bookmarklet-menu-item"], which opens a dialog with the bookmarklet to drag. 5. That dialog's link has the same href: eval document.querySelector('[data-testid=bookmarklet-link]')?.getAttribute('href') === window.__href expecting true. Then hand the link to the host page with eval fetch('http://host.test/bookmarklet', { method: 'POST', body: window.__href }).then((r) => r.ok) expecting true. Navigate tab "host" to http://host.test/. In tab "host", select the paragraph: eval getSelection().selectAllChildren(document.getElementById('para')). In tab "host", click the bookmarklet as if in the bookmarks bar: eval fetch('/bookmarklet').then((r) => r.text()).then((href) => { location.href = href; }). In tab "host", the toolbar status should be visible with exactly the text "Linked". Then perform these steps in order: 1. In the Shelley window, [data-testid="message-input"] must have the value exactly {{PAGE}}. 2. A pick from Shelley's own origin, not the linked page, is dropped: in the Shelley window, eval window.postMessage({ tag: 'shelley-bookmarklet', type: 'pick', pick: { url: 'https://evil.test/', selector: 'x', html: 'x' } }, '*'). 3. In tab "host", click the toolbar's "Pick" button, then click the page's h1. 4. In the Shelley window, the message input's value must be exactly {{PICKED_H1}} (the h1's pick and nothing from evil.test). 5. Clicking the toolbar while picking works the toolbar: in tab "host", click the toolbar's "Pick" button; it must have the attribute aria-pressed exactly "true". 6. Click it again; its aria-pressed must be exactly "false". 7. Click it once more (picking again), then click the toolbar's "Close" button. 8. In tab "host", there must be exactly 0 "shelley-bookmarklet" elements. 9. In tab "host", click the h1. 10. With picking off, that click reaches the page (picking swallows clicks, so the page has counted none on its h1 before): in tab "host", eval window.__h1Clicks expecting 1. 11. In the Shelley window, the message input's value must still be exactly {{PICKED_H1}}.

steps.expression: window.postMessage({ tag: 'shelley-bookmarklet', type: 'pick', pick: { url: 'https://evil.test/', selector: 'x', html: 'x' } }, '*')
